text_summary.body: In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar came up and Jehoiakim served him three years before rebelling; bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites and Ammonites were sent against Judah.

setting.body: After Carchemish (605) the Babylonian Chronicle records Nebuchadnezzar's yearly campaigns in Ḫatti; it records no siege of Jerusalem before 597. In 601 Nebuchadnezzar fought Egypt with heavy losses on both sides (ABC 5), a likely occasion for a vassal's revolt.

competing_reconstructions.label: Submission in 605/604 (Dan 1:1 campaign)
competing_reconstructions.summary: The three years of service began after Carchemish when Nebuchadnezzar's army overran Ḫatti; Dan 1:1 records the same campaign.

competing_reconstructions.label: Submission in 604/603 (Ashkelon campaign) or later
competing_reconstructions.summary: The chronicle's campaign of Kislev 604 (Ashkelon) is another occasion; the identity of the Dan 1:1 event with 2 Kgs 24:1 is under review on the Dan 1 record.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik places Nebuchadnezzar's first strike in 605, when "a few choice captives (such as Daniel)" were taken.
